world.title: In 1929, a fisherman built a wooden boat beside the home where he was raising 13 children; nearly a century later, $1.5 million is being raised to restore it
world.summary: A wooden fishing boat named Little Lady, built in 1929 on Martha’s Vineyard, is undergoing a significant restoration. The boat, the last of its kind, is set to be moved to the Gannon and Benjamin Marine Railway for repairs. A fundraising effort has raised $1.5 million to support the restoration project, preserving its historical significance.

world.title: New strategy will shatter your foundations, Iran’s top security official warns US
world.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Major General Mohsen Rezaei warned the United States that its efforts to salvage the ongoing conflict will be unsuccessful. He stated that a newly adopted Iranian strategy is designed to dismantle U.S. influence and operations in the region. Rezaei emphasized that the U.S. should reconsider its approach to avoid further failures.

world.title: 'You'll soon see': Iran vows ‘new strategy’ against US as six-month war sees heaviest exchange in weeks
world.summary: Iran has announced a “new strategy” against the US amid escalating conflict in the Middle East. The warning follows a significant increase in fighting, with Iran condemning a recent US airstrike on a wedding in Sirik as a “war crime.” The situation reflects heightened tensions and ongoing military exchanges between the two nations over the past six months.

business.title: Uber lays off 3,300 employees as it restructures for faster growth
business.summary: Uber Technologies announced it will lay off approximately 3,300 employees, accounting for about 10% of its global workforce. This decision is part of a significant restructuring initiative aimed at streamlining operations and enhancing growth. The layoffs reflect the company's efforts to reduce management layers and improve efficiency as it navigates challenges in the competitive ride-hailing market.

business.title: Uber to cut 10% of global workforce, 3,300 jobs in major restructuring: Report
business.summary: Uber plans to reduce its global workforce by 10%, resulting in approximately 3,300 job cuts as part of a major restructuring effort. The company will decrease its number of managers by 20%, with some managers transitioning to individual contributor roles. An Uber spokesperson confirmed these changes, which aim to streamline operations and improve efficiency within the organization.

business.title: Simple Wave Electric Scooter Launch Price Rs 1.10 Lakh in India
business.summary: The Simple Wave electric scooter has been launched in India at an introductory price of Rs 1.10 lakh. It offers multiple battery pack options, including 2.2 kWh, 2.7 kWh, 3.7 kWh, and 5 kWh. The scooter aims to cater to various consumer needs in the growing electric vehicle market, providing flexibility in battery capacity choices.

technology.title: Optoma Launches N-Series 4K Professional Displays in India
technology.summary: Optoma India has introduced its N-Series Professional Displays, featuring commercial-grade 4K UHD screens tailored for businesses and organizations needing high-quality visuals and smart content management. The displays, available in sizes of 55-inch, 65-inch, 75-inch, 86-inch, and 98-inch, are designed for continuous 24/7 operation and are suitable for various environments, including retail stores and hotels.

technology.title: Indian scientists break a century-old limit on turning heat into electricity
technology.summary: Indian scientists have achieved a significant breakthrough by generating a large electrical voltage from a small temperature difference, challenging a century-old limit in solid material science. This discovery could lead to advancements in sensing heat and detecting extremely weak light. The research opens new possibilities for applications in various fields, enhancing the understanding of thermoelectric effects in materials.

technology.title: Sonos expands headphone range with Ace Ultra, successor to original Sonos Ace
technology.summary: Sonos has introduced the Ace Ultra, an over-ear headphone that succeeds the original Sonos Ace. The new model features a redesigned driver, a 10-microphone noise-cancelling system, and can link with other headphones. It offers up to 35 hours of battery life, enhancing the listening experience with improved sound quality and advanced noise cancellation technology.

sports.title: Five free agents Chelsea could sign to replace Enzo Fernandez after transfer drama
sports.summary: Chelsea is exploring the free agent market to find a replacement for Enzo Fernandez before their upcoming match against Arsenal. Following a disappointing end to the summer transfer window, the club is considering several options. The potential signings aim to bolster the squad and address the gap left by Fernandez's departure, ensuring competitiveness in the upcoming fixtures.

sports.title: Marc Marquez “would have been first from Turn 1” at Aragon MotoGP
sports.summary: Marc Marquez expressed confidence that he would have led every lap at the Aragon MotoGP if not for a mistake with his ride-height device. He felt he could have replicated his Sprint performance, stating he would have been first from Turn 1. Marquez shared these thoughts in a recent Inside Ducati YouTube video, discussing his race experience.

sports.title: The 10 free agents who are still without a club including Sancho, Sterling, Pogba and Alaba
sports.summary: Several high-profile football players remain without a club following the closure of the summer transfer window. Notable free agents include Jadon Sancho, Raheem Sterling, Paul Pogba, and David Alaba. Meanwhile, Premier League clubs set a new summer spending record of approximately £3.46 billion, acquiring players like Enzo Fernandez and Bradley Barcola, alongside significant signings across other European leagues.

health.title: Is It Okay to Eat the Same Thing Every Day? Experts Reveal the Consequences
health.summary: An explainer discusses the implications of eating the same meals daily, focusing on mental energy and long-term health. It highlights potential nutritional deficiencies and their effects on overall well-being. The article also emphasizes the importance of dietary variety for maintaining gut microbiome diversity, as reported by the American Gut Project, suggesting that routine eating may have significant health consequences.

health.title: India Sees Growing Cases of Fatty Liver and Colorectal Cancer
health.summary: India is experiencing an increase in metabolic gastrointestinal diseases, notably fatty liver disease and colorectal cancer. These health issues are rising despite ongoing challenges from persistent infections like Helicobacter pylori and intestinal worm infestations. The growing prevalence of these conditions highlights the need for improved healthcare strategies to address both metabolic diseases and infectious diseases affecting communities across the country.

health.title: Ebola death toll passes 3,000 in DR Congo: official data
health.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 3,000 deaths, marking it the deadliest outbreak recorded. The World Health Organization has recommended initiating clinical trials for the Ervebo vaccine in response to the crisis. The epidemic primarily affects the conflict-affected eastern and northeastern regions of the country, exacerbating the ongoing humanitarian challenges.

science.title: NASA's 10 most beautiful, sparkly images of dead stars captured by the Hubble Space Telescope
science.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has released stunning images of dying stars, supernova remnants, and glowing nebulae. These visuals highlight the universe's dramatic cosmic transformations, showcasing the beauty and complexity of stellar evolution. The collection emphasizes Hubble's capability to capture intricate details of celestial phenomena, contributing to our understanding of the life cycles of stars and their remnants.

science.title: CERN upgrades Large Hadron Collider to pursue dark matter discoveries
science.summary: CERN is upgrading the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) to investigate dark matter, which constitutes over a quarter of the universe yet remains invisible. This initiative follows their landmark discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012. The upgraded LHC aims to enhance the search for answers regarding dark matter, a significant focus in contemporary physics research.

science.title: STAT3-derived EIF4E3 promotes H2O2-induced human trabecular meshwork cell injury by activating TGF-β-SMAD2/3 pathway
science.summary: The study investigates EIF4E3's role in human trabecular meshwork (HTM) cell injury related to glaucoma. H2O2-treated HTM cells were used to simulate oxidative stress. Results showed that STAT3 promotes EIF4E3 expression, activating the TGF-β-SMAD2/3 pathway, which leads to apoptosis and oxidative injury. EIF4E3 knockdown mitigated these effects, indicating its potential involvement in glaucoma pathogenesis.

entertainment.title: 'Hanuman Ansh' vs 'Dhurandhar 2': How Rs 2 crore spiritual biopic on Neem Karoli Baba has surpassed Ranveer Singh's blockbuster in return on investment and delivered over 20x returns despite opening a
entertainment.summary: The spiritual biopic "Hanuman Ansh," produced for Rs 2 crore, has outperformed the blockbuster "Dhurandhar 2" in terms of return on investment, achieving over 20 times its production cost. This unexpected success highlights the diverse landscape of the Indian box office in 2026, where smaller films can achieve significant financial milestones against larger productions.

entertainment.title: Rajkumar Hirani confirms '3 Idiots' sequel casting 'will be the same', reveals story is set 20 years later: 'It’s not about the students'
entertainment.summary: Filmmaker Rajkumar Hirani has provided an update on the sequel to his 2009 film '3 Idiots', confirming that the original cast will return. The story is set 20 years later and will not focus on the students. Hirani stated that the script is currently being written, but the project is still in the early stages of development.

entertainment.title: 'Ramba Ho' actress Kalpana Iyer says she's ghosted after requesting for work: 'Just a 70-year old saying be decent and fair, at least inform me'
entertainment.summary: Veteran actress Kalpana Iyer expressed disappointment over being ignored after requesting work opportunities. She highlighted her feelings of hurt, stating that as a 70-year-old, she deserves decency and fairness in professional interactions. Iyer recently gained attention for a video of her dancing to her famous song “Rambha Ho” at a friend's wedding, marking her return to the spotlight.
